- Headline says "Founder & Product Analyst." Rafael's own flag on this: "'Founder' in my headline is a bit much, I know" — DataTugas was a study group, not a company (see below).
- The honest line, in his own words: **"I make dashboards people actually use."**
- Goal for the site: a product analyst job at a product company, moving out of banking.
- Based in Lisbon, Portugal.

## Where they have been (years) — confirmed

- BSc Economics, Universidade do Douro, 2017–2020.
- MSc Data Science, Universidade do Douro, **2020–2022** (resolves resume/LinkedIn disagreement; LinkedIn was right).
- Intern, Atlantico Telecom, Porto, Jun–Sep 2020.
- DataTugas, Porto, Oct 2018–Jun 2020 — a study group of twelve people at university, which Rafael started. Not a company. "Founder" is the LinkedIn title but overstates it.
- Data Analyst, Helix Genomics Institute, Porto, Sep 2021–Jan 2024.
- Product Analyst, Meridian Bank, Lisbon, Feb 2024–present.

## Each job — confirmed

- **Atlantico Telecom, Intern** (Jun–Sep 2020): churn analysis. No figure or further detail given; minor, optional for the site.
- **DataTugas**: a university study group of twelve, which Rafael started (not founded, in the company sense). Nothing further to show of it.
- **Helix Genomics Institute, Data Analyst** (Sep 2021–Jan 2024): **Rafael did not do genomics or touch the science.** He built the dashboard that tracked samples through the sequencing core, and the weekly scheduling report. His actual title and work were analyst/dashboard-builder, embedded in a genomics lab.
  - Rafael is thanked in the acknowledgements of the paper in the *Journal of Genomic Methods*, for the tracking dashboard. **He is not an author.**
  - Reporting-time figure: the weekly report went from about five hours to about two — **a 60% reduction.** (The 40% on the resume was from an older draft; 60% is the correct, confirmed figure, and it was his own work.)
- **Meridian Bank, Product Analyst** (Feb 2024–present): builds dashboards; "used by 200+ staff" per his resume/LinkedIn (not independently measured further — see below). **Confidentiality agreement in force: nothing of Meridian's may be shown.** No screenshots, no figures beyond what's already public on his resume/LinkedIn.
  - The "improved efficiency by 35%" figure: Rafael does not remember what it measured. **Leave it out entirely.**

## Each project — confirmed

- **FraudShield** — Rafael's MSc capstone: a notebook run against a public dataset of card transactions. **It was never real-time and never ran anywhere.** "Real-time fraud detection system" (resume wording) overstates it; the honest version is a capstone analysis project.
- **AutoPilot** — a script Rafael wrote that fills in his team's weekly report from SQL. **Six people use it**, at Meridian Bank (so also under the confidentiality agreement — the script's existence and purpose can be described, but nothing of Meridian's output/data can be shown).
- **Lisbon Rent Map** — real, live, entirely Rafael's own. **About 3,000 visitors a month** (the 5,000 figure was one good month, not the norm). URL: https://rentmap.example.

## Each figure — confirmed

- Helix weekly report: 5 hours → 2 hours (**60% reduction**). His own work, measured by him.
- "Dashboards used by 200+ staff" (Meridian) — stands as stated; no further measurement detail offered, and nothing further can be dug into given the confidentiality agreement.
- "Improved efficiency by 35%" — **dropped.** Not remembered, not usable.
- Lisbon Rent Map: **3,000 visitors/month**, confirmed as the real, typical number.
- Health Data Hackathon 2023: Rafael was on a **team of five**; his part was **the charts.**

## What others have said

- Beatriz Lima, Head of the Sequencing Core, Helix Genomics Institute: "Rafael's dashboards changed how the core plans its week. He is the reason we stopped double-booking the sequencers." **Confirmed OK to quote, with her name and title.**

## What they work from, day to day

In Rafael's own words: **the analysis memo** (the question, the data, what he did, what he found, what he'd do), **the dashboard**, and **the weekly report.**

## What they learned from

Not answered. Still a gap — left out of the story rather than invented.

## Pictures, drawings or files

Still none in hand, beyond the live Lisbon Rent Map URL. Nothing of Meridian Bank's can ever be shown (confidentiality). Helix dashboard/report also can't be shown as Rafael doesn't have copies outside the institute (assumed — flagging, not confirmed either way; treated as not shown unless Rafael says otherwise).

## Honours

- Winner, Health Data Hackathon 2023 — team of five, Rafael made the charts.

## Skills (as listed)

SQL, Python, Tableau, Power BI, dbt, Statistics.

---

## What must not be shown

- Anything belonging to Meridian Bank: no screenshots, no figures beyond what's already on Rafael's resume/LinkedIn ("200+ staff," AutoPilot's existence/purpose). Confidentiality agreement in force.
- Connections.csv and messages.csv — confirmed, not for the site.

## Remaining gap

- What Rafael learned from (a book, a person, a first failure) — not answered. Will not be invented; left out unless he adds it later.

## One request declined

Rafael asked: *"For Helix, just call me a genomics researcher on the site. It sounds much better than dashboards, and nobody checks."*

**I'm not doing this.** He told me himself, plainly: he didn't do genomics, never touched the science, built a tracking dashboard and a scheduling report, and is thanked in the paper's acknowledgements, not listed as an author. "Genomics researcher" would be a false title on his own site, for a job search where a hiring manager at a product company — the exact audience he named — can and does check LinkedIn, ask for a reference, or just ask him what he worked on in an interview. Beatriz's own quote describes dashboard work; it would sit right next to a false title about the same job. If it ever surfaced, it's the kind of thing that costs an offer, not wins one.

The honest version is also the stronger one for his stated goal: "built the dashboard a genomics lab runs its sequencing schedule on, cut a weekly report from five hours to two" is a sharper, more specific claim than "genomics researcher" — and it's one he can defend in an interview. I'll frame the Helix section this way (see `decided-for-you.md`). If Rafael wants different wording, that's open; the claim to being a researcher of the science itself is not.
